1.title: The Birth and Expansion of the Grand Cru Classification
1.html:
20 November 1975 — a decree formally creates the Alsace Grand Cru classification
23 November 1983 — the first 25 Grand Cru sites are delimited
1992 — another 25 are delimited, bringing the total to 50
2007 — the 51st Grand Cru, "Kaefferkopf" (Ammerschwihr), is formally delimited — also the only Grand Cru that allowed blends from the very beginning

Grand Cru makes up only about 4% of Alsace's total output, the rarest tier at the top of the pyramid; the 51 sites are spread across the hills of Bas-Rhin (14) and Haut-Rhin (37).
2.title: Core Grand Cru Rules
2.html:
• Variety restriction: in principle a single noble variety — one of Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris or Muscat
  • Two blending exceptions: Altenberg de Bergheim (Riesling + Pinot Gris + Gewurztraminer) and Kaefferkopf (Gewurztraminer + Riesling + Pinot Gris)
  • Hand harvesting: mandatory for all 51 Grand Crus
  • Yield limit: base 55 hl/ha, PLC up to 20% more, maximum 66 hl/ha
  • The label must show both: the site name (lieu-dit) + the vintage — both are required
  • Bottling in the region of origin: mandatory, as for all Alsace wines

💡 Grand Cru sites vary enormously in size — the smallest, Kanzlerberg, is only 3.23 hectares, while the largest, Schlossberg, reaches 80.28 hectares, reflecting the natural boundaries of each site's terroir rather than a tidy man-made division.
3.question: From its creation in 1975 to the final 51 sites in 2007, in how many waves was the Alsace Grand Cru classification delimited?
3.options.0: All 51 at once, with no later adjustment
3.options.1: Three waves: 25 in 1983, another 25 in 1992, and the 51st (Kaefferkopf) in 2007
3.options.2: One or two added every year, continuing to this day
3.options.3: Two waves: 30 in 1975 and another 21 in 1992
3.explanation: The Grand Cru classification was delimited in three waves: the first 25 on 23 November 1983, another 25 in 1992 (50 in total), and the 51st, Kaefferkopf, in 2007 — also the only Grand Cru that allowed blends from the very beginning.
